summary: Same Matrix-rain-plus-pulse pattern with an identical palette and glyph vocabulary, but the port runs its whole event cadence exactly 1.50x slower (3.93 s vs 2.62 s), loops on a different phrase length (39.35 s vs 13.10 s), and sits fully dark ~45% of the time against the original's ~28%.
observations: Default rig is strip/60px (manifest); both sides compile and run clean on every rig tried (strip 60, grid 8x8, 16x16, 32x32, 48x48) with no compile or runtime errors, and neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both).

Shared visual vocabulary: on a 32x32/48x48 grid both draw slanted rows of short green/cyan 'code' dashes whose slope and dash size evolve, punctuated by bright horizontal 'pulse' blooms that sweep the rig. On the 60px strip both read as curved feather/frond bundles of diagonal dashes plus periodic lens-shaped bright blooms (regime-gappy: orig bloom at t=8.2-9.3 s spanning px ~2-38; port bloom at t=8.3-9.4 s spanning px ~0-14).

TEMPO (headline): autocorrelation of meanBrightness on the 240 s / 5 fps survey gives the original an event ladder at 2.70, 5.05, 8.10, 10.35, 13.10, 15.70, 18.15, 21.20, 23.45, 26.20, 28.70 s (base interval ~2.62 s) and the port a ladder at 3.90, 7.90, 11.80, 15.75, 19.70, 23.55, 27.55 s (base interval ~3.93 s). 3.93 / 2.62 = 1.50 exactly.

TEMPO confirmed by global time-warp: aligning orig meanBrightness(t) against port meanBrightness(scale*t + offset) over 240 s peaks sharply at scale = 1.50 (r = 0.616, offset 23.8 s); r <= 0.164 at scale 1.00, 1.25, 1.333, 1.667 and 2.00. The port plays the same temporal envelope at 2/3 speed.
TEMPO is rig-independent: the same 2.6 s (orig) vs 3.9 s (port) ladders appear on a 16x16 grid rig over 120 s @ 10 fps (grid16-long), so it is not a strip-mapping artefact.

LOOP LENGTH: the original repeats essentially exactly every 13.10 s (ACF 0.88 at 13.2 s, 0.88 at 78.6 s = 6 loops, 0.95 at 91.8 s = 7 loops, 0.89 at 104.8 s = 8 loops) — i.e. a 5-event, 13.1 s phrase. The port repeats every 39.35 s (ACF 0.98 at 39.4 s, 0.99 at 78.6 s, 0.99 at 118.0 s) — a 10-event phrase. Even after correcting for the 1.5x tempo the port's phrase is twice as long as the original's.

PHRASING CHARACTER: at a one-event lag the original's ACF is only 0.31 (successive events differ from each other) while the port's is 0.60-0.70 (successive events are near-copies). The port reads metronomic; the original has internal variety inside its 13.1 s phrase.

DUTY CYCLE: over 60 s @ 20 fps the original is fully black on 241/1200 frames (20%) and at meanBrightness <= 1 on 28% of frames, longest all-black run 1.35 s. The port is black on 418/1200 (35%), <=1 on 45%, longest all-black run 2.05 s. Same numbers on the 240 s survey: orig lit 70% of frames, port 55%.

DARK-GAP LAYOUT: over 0-60 s the original's dark gaps (mean <= 1 for >= 0.5 s) start at 6.3, 9.2, 11.8, 19.4, 22.4, 24.9, 32.6, 35.5, 37.9, 45.7, 48.5, 50.9 s — three gaps per 13.1 s loop followed by a ~7.6 s continuously-lit passage. The port's start at 1.6, 5.6, 9.3, 13.5, 17.3, 21.7, 25.1, 29.3, 33.3, 37.5, 40.9, 45.0, 48.6, 52.9, 56.6 s — one gap every 3.93 s, evenly spaced, with no long lit passage anywhere.

BRIGHTNESS: mean brightness averaged only over LIT frames is nearly identical (orig 9.72, port 9.56; p90 19 vs 18), so the port is not globally scaled down — it is dark more of the time. Peaks do differ though: orig peaks reach mean 39-41 (t=21.5 s, 8.4 s, 34.6 s) while the port tops out at 25-28 (t=36.4 s, 20.5 s), about 30% lower.

COLOR: hue histograms over 23 sampled frames are near-identical. Both occupy hue 30-270 deg only (yellow / green / cyan / blue / violet), zero pixels in 0-30 or 270-360 (no reds or magentas), and both are fully saturated (mean saturation 1.00). Per-30-deg-bin difference is <= 3.6 pp. Mean value of lit pixels 49 (orig) vs 41 (port). Channel averages orig R 2.63 / G 11.70 / B 6.37 vs port R 2.39 / G 9.22 / B 4.47 — the port's B:G ratio is slightly lower (0.485 vs 0.545).

GLYPH SHAPE: on a 32x32 grid, sampled every 0.5 s over 40 s, the original's lit runs average 5.89 px horizontally and 1.70 px vertically (aspect 3.46); the port's average 7.82 px horizontally and 1.42 px vertically (aspect 5.49). The port's dashes are longer and thinner — more like continuous horizontal streaks, less like the original's chunky blocks. Fill fraction while lit is comparable (0.293 vs 0.320).

MOTION DIRECTION/SPEED on the strip: circular cross-correlation of consecutive frames dumped every 0.1 s across 0-30 s gives both sides a leftward drift, orig mean -5.7 px/s, port mean -4.3 px/s; both distributions are dominated by 0-px frames with a tail at -1 to -3 px per 0.1 s. Same direction, port ~25% slower, consistent with the overall tempo deficit.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING: none on either side. The ACF ladders are identical at 5, 10 and 20 fps (orig 13.10/13.10/13.20 s; port 15.70/15.75/15.80 s), so both engines are time-based and the tempo divergence is a real port bug, not an fps artefact.

SEED: both sides are fully deterministic and seed-independent — seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give byte-identical statsSummary and identical ACF ladders on both sides. So every difference reported here is structural, not an RNG draw.

STEADY STATE: at t = 120-150 s (late-steady, 30 s @ 10 fps) both sides are still alive with the same character — orig meanBrightness avg 7.1 (max 34), port avg 5.0 (max 25); neither decays to black or saturates. brightnessTrend 'volatile' on both, which for this pattern just reflects the pulse structure. No time-degeneracy on either side.

RESOLUTION: both sides are resolution-DEPENDENT in the same way — feature counts and dash sizes scale with the grid (8x8 shows a handful of coarse dashes; 48x48 shows dozens of fine rows). No structural mismatch on this axis.
CONTROL SURFACE: both sides expose zero controls (meta.json controls: [] on orig and port; --probe-controls reports 'no settable controls' for both). Surfaces match; nothing dropped or invented.
feedback: Primary fix: the port's animation clock runs at 2/3 the original's rate. Every event on the port takes 3.93 s where the original takes 2.62 s, and a global time-warp fit over 240 s picks scale 1.50 with r=0.62 against r<=0.16 at every other scale tested. Speeding the port's time base up by exactly 1.5x should bring cadence, drift speed (-4.3 -> -5.7 px/s) and pulse rate into line in one move.

Second fix: phrase length. Even after correcting the tempo, the original's animation repeats EXACTLY every 13.10 s (5 events) while the port repeats every 39.35 s (10 events). After the 1.5x speed-up the port would loop at 26.2 s, still 2x the original's phrase. Whatever counter or modulus governs the loop should be halved so the whole thing closes after 5 events / 13.1 s.

Third fix: duty cycle. The port is completely dark 35% of frames against the original's 20% (45% vs 28% at meanBrightness <= 1), and its longest continuous blackout is 2.05 s against 1.35 s. Critically, the original has a ~7.6 s stretch inside each 13.1 s loop with NO dark gap at all — a sustained busy passage — while the port drops to black once every single 3.93 s event with no exception. The port needs a mode/phase where consecutive events overlap instead of each fading fully out.

Fourth fix: peak amplitude. The original's bright pulses reach mean brightness 39-41; the port's cap at 25-28, about 30% low. Note that average brightness over LIT frames already matches (9.72 vs 9.56), so do NOT scale the whole pattern up — only the pulse/bloom peak is short. On the strip the original's bloom at t=8.2-9.3 s spans ~36 px; the port's at the same moment spans only ~14 px, so the bloom's spatial extent is short too and may be the same knob.

Fifth (minor) fix: glyph aspect. On a 32x32 grid the port's dashes average 7.8 px long and 1.4 px thick (aspect 5.5) versus the original's 5.9 x 1.7 (aspect 3.5). The port's 'code' streaks should be ~25% shorter and ~20% thicker to read as blocks rather than lines.

Sixth (minor) fix: event variety. Consecutive events on the port are near-copies of each other (autocorrelation 0.60-0.70 at one-event lag) while the original's differ substantially (0.31). Whatever per-event parameter the original varies across its 5-event phrase (slope, dash size and density all visibly change frame to frame in the 48x48 sheet) is being held closer to constant in the port.

Do NOT change: palette (hue span 30-270 deg, full saturation, no reds — matches within 3.6 pp per bin), motion direction (both drift left), fps-independence (both correct), determinism (both seed-independent), control surface (both correctly have zero dials), and steady-state stability (both fine at t=120-150 s).
